xmldoc.short_description: Tells if daylight saving time is in effect in a time zone at given serial date numbers.

param_input_item.param_description: a numeric array: serial date numbers (see datenum), read as wall-clock times of tz.
a string: time zone name (for example 'Europe/Paris', 'UTC', 'local', '+05:30' or a POSIX TZ rule).
a string: folder of the time zone database to use. An empty value keeps the current setting.

param_output_item.param_description: a logical array of the same size as dn: true where daylight saving time applies.
a double array of the same size as dn: daylight saving shift in seconds included in the UTC offset (0 in standard time).

description.p: timezonedst returns true for each serial date number of dn at which the time zone tz observes daylight saving time.
It is a low-level function used by isdst. Most scripts should call isdst on a datetime instead.
Time zone names are read as in timezoneoffset. UTC and fixed offsets such as '+05:30' never observe daylight saving time. Non-finite values of dn give false.
When dataPath is given, it becomes the database folder of all the time zone functions for the rest of the session. An unknown time zone raises an error.
The second output shift gives the real shift, for example 1800 for a 30 minute rule. Non-finite values of dn give 0.

example_item.example_item_description: Daylight saving time in New York in winter and in summer.
